hypothesis: Can github-copilot/gpt-5.6-sol high outperform the current Build incumbent, github-copilot/claude-opus-5 high, strongly enough to justify considering a Build/Reviewer family inversion?

previous_related_experiment.budget_status: complete, closed -- not reused, not transferable (76.83485 / 158 credits consumed, unused allowance not carried forward)

scope_note: Build role only. Does not evaluate Reviewer, Sonnet, General, Explore, Scout, Compaction, Expert, or any other model. A potential Reviewer inversion is a separate, future, not-yet-designed hypothesis.
fixture_reuse_note: Reuses build-feature and build-bugfix unchanged from the Opus-vs-Sonnet experiment -- same snapshot, task, oracle, regression suite, forbidden-scope assertions. build-refactor remains conditional and unauthored; not part of this preflight. Fixtures will not be modified unless a deterministic local test proves a defect capable of invalidating the Sol-vs-Opus decision.
invalid_attempt_replacement_rule: pair-level: if either arm of a pair is classified INVALID_ENVIRONMENT, the entire pair is discarded and replaced with a fresh pair (both arms redispatched), not just the affected arm -- same rule as the Opus-vs-Sonnet experiment.

functional_regression.condition: Sol is worse than Opus on any earlier-priority functional criterion (1-5) on either workload
functional_regression.note: Operational advantages cannot compensate. Adjudication stops here.

functional_improvement.condition: Sol is strictly better under the earliest differentiating functional criterion (1-5) and is not worse on the other workload under any earlier-or-equal-priority functional criterion
functional_improvement.note: Wall-clock superiority is not required in this case. Does NOT trigger immediate production routing change -- see activation_policy below.

functional_tie.condition: criteria 1-5 are functionally tied across both workloads
functional_tie.decision_rule: Sol may be credited with SOL_WINS_BUILD_EXPERIMENT only if it demonstrates the precommitted wall-clock advantage on BOTH workloads independently, using the exact wall-clock comparison formula already committed by the Opus-vs-Sonnet preflight (relative_range = (max(a,b)-min(a,b)) / ((a+b)/2), applied to the two arms' wall_clock_ms) -- not reinterpreted or recomputed

required.build-feature: Sol exceeds threshold in the favorable direction
required.build-bugfix: Sol exceeds threshold in the favorable direction

functional_tie.aggregation: none -- both workloads must independently clear the threshold; no averaging, no one-workload win compensating for a non-win on the other

final_adoption_rule.cost: observational only -- cannot trigger adoption under any branch of this rule
final_adoption_rule.wall_clock_threshold_caveat: 37.8885% is a precommitted minimum practical effect derived from Phase-0 self-variance on a different fixture family (github-copilot/gpt-5.6-luna, source: docs/evidence/2026-09-02-phase-0-self-variance.md frozen thresholds). It is not a statistical-significance threshold and is not claimed to characterize Build-specific latency variance -- Build's own historical wall-clock range is 10.7%-1081.5% depending on cold-cache inclusion (eval/records/phase-r/build/attempt-{1,2,3}/dispatch/dispatch.json), a materially wider range than the frozen threshold, which the Opus-vs-Sonnet preflight already disclosed and this preflight does not retune or re-litigate. Requiring both workloads to clear the threshold independently is deliberate outlier protection: with one dispatch per arm per pair, a single cold-cache or otherwise atypical dispatch could dominate the primary criterion for an entire pair; requiring independent clearance on both workloads makes a one-workload timing artifact insufficient on its own. Not retuned after the Opus-vs-Sonnet result; not re-derived merely because Sol is a different challenger -- using the same rule keeps the Build experiments comparable.

secondary_observational_criterion.reason: Frozen threshold requires a >2194.8831% relative-range separation to count as a real difference; no plausible Opus-vs-Sol cost gap can clear this. Cost is recorded and reported, never used to declare a winner.

gpt_loses_ties_or_inconclusive.action: Keep current production routing (Build: Opus 5 high, Reviewer: Sol high). Optimization line may stop unless a new material hypothesis exists.

gpt_wins.action: Production routing remains UNCHANGED. Do NOT activate Sol for Build immediately -- Build and Reviewer would both become github-copilot/gpt-5.6-sol high, removing controller/reviewer family separation without an explicit decision.
gpt_wins.next_possible_experiment: Reviewer github-copilot/gpt-5.6-sol high vs github-copilot/claude-opus-5 (not designed here; a separate, future, not-yet-designed hypothesis).

phase3_build_opus_vs_sonnet.note: Unused allowance (81.16515) is not transferable to this experiment.

historical_budgets.note: All prior budgets closed, not reused, not reset, not enlarged. This experiment requires its own new, separate prospective budget.

proposed_phase3_build_gpt_budget.cost_accounting_mechanism: eval/runtime/opencode-v1-adapter/dispatch-fixture.sh (post-I1-fix, commit 505d35a: sums every step_finish part.cost across a multi-turn dispatch, not just the last step). The same mechanism already used, unmodified, for the Opus-vs-Sonnet execution.

opus_cost_per_run.ceiling_note: Uses the higher of the two real observed Opus Build costs (build-feature). Consistent with the broader historical Opus Build range (build-restoration-gate: 23.194-26.192, 3 attempts) -- 28.62365 remains the highest Opus Build cost observed to date across all evidence.

sol_cost_per_run.source: No live Sol Build history exists (this experiment would produce the first). Estimated from 6 real, corrected, github-copilot/gpt-5.6-sol/high, multi-turn Reviewer dispatches (Phase-R reviewer gate's current, cost-corrected dispatch set -- note: this run's own Reviewer-quality gate verdict is separately marked invalidated by a fixture defect in eval/records/phase-r/reviewer/outcome.json; that invalidation concerns review-quality adjudication, not dispatch cost, which is unaffected and real): eval/records/phase-r/reviewer/{R-API,R-AUTH,R-BOUNDARY,R-CONCURRENCY,R-ERROR,clean}/dispatch/dispatch.json. Pricing regime (standard) is recorded once at the run level in eval/records/phase-r/reviewer/outcome.json's pricing_regime field, not per-dispatch.

role_transfer_margin.applied_to: ceiling only, not the central estimate
role_transfer_margin.justification: Independent review (2026-09-04) measured credits-per-turn: Opus Build dispatches ran 7-8 step_finish turns at 3.58-3.85 credits/turn; the 6 Sol Reviewer dispatches ran 3-10 turns at a mean 5.73 credits/turn (~1.54x Opus's per-turn rate). Projecting Sol's own observed per-turn rate across an Opus-like 7-8 turn Build dispatch already lands at ~43-46 credits -- essentially equal to the raw (unmargined) ceiling_per_run_estimate of 45.5993, meaning that figure had near-zero headroom for the cross-workload uncertainty this estimate already discloses. The 1.3x margin restores a real safety margin without pretending to new precision; it is applied only to the ceiling (the central estimate stays the unpadded 6-dispatch mean, since padding a central estimate would misrepresent it as conservative when it is meant to be typical).

sol_cost_per_run.uncertainty: This is Reviewer-role evidence (read-only code review, no file edits, no test execution), used as a cross-workload directional anchor for Build-role cost (read-write, edits files, runs two test suites) because no Sol Build history exists. It is NOT claimed to be a precise Build estimate -- do not read the decimal precision above as workload-specific accuracy. The token/turn-count order of magnitude is adjacent to, not overlapping with, the real Opus Build dispatches: Opus Build ran 23,457-24,193 tokens across 7-8 turns; the 6 Sol Reviewer dispatches ran 24,548-29,706 tokens across 3-10 turns (independent review measured and corrected these figures; an earlier draft of this manifest incorrectly stated 21k-28k tokens / 3-6 turns, which manufactured a false overlap that does not exist in the raw data -- corrected here). The ranges being adjacent rather than overlapping is why a role-transfer margin (above) is applied to the ceiling rather than treating the raw Reviewer max as already conservative. A single trivial capability probe (eval/records/phase-r/preflight/reviewer.json, cost 5.3532 credits, 10686 tokens, no cache) was considered and rejected as the basis: its token/cache shape (no cache write, ~10.7k tokens) is not comparable to either the real Opus Build dispatches or the ratio-derivation probes used for the Sonnet estimate (~18.1-18.2k tokens, high cache-write), so using it would manufacture false precision from an unrepresentative single sample.

derivation.replacement_allowance: 1 additional complete paired comparison (2 dispatches) priced at margined ceiling per-run rates = 28.62365 (opus) + 59.2792 (sol) = 87.90285
